sections.title: Article 1 - Introduction and Data Controller
paragraphs: This Privacy Policy (hereinafter the "**Policy**") explains how **YUMNI SAS** (hereinafter "**we**", "**YUMNI**") collects, uses, processes and protects personal data when you use the YUMNI platform (hereinafter the "**Platform**"), a SaaS solution for managing Corporate Social Responsibility strategy, accessible at https://yumni.fr/fr.

paragraphsAfter: We are committed to respecting and protecting your personal data in strict compliance with **Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of 27 April 2016** on the protection of personal data (hereinafter the "**GDPR**") and with **Law No. 78-17 of 6 January 1978** on data processing, files and individual liberties (the "Informatique et Libertés" Act), as currently in force.

The YUMNI Platform is a solution for **exclusively professional (B2B)** use, intended for legal entities and natural persons acting in the course of their professional activity. subsections.note: **Important:** YUMNI SAS processes these operational CSR data in the capacity of **data processor** within the meaning of Article 28 of the GDPR. The Customer (the subscribing organisation) remains the data controller for these data. If these data contain nominal references to third parties (employees, contractors, partners), it is the Customer's responsibility to ensure their lawfulness and to inform the data subjects accordingly. For a full explanation of this dual role, see Article 4.

subsections.title: 2.4 Enhanced authentication data (MFA)

Ten (10) single-use backup codes, individually hashed
Opaque fingerprint of the memorised trusted device, transmitted via **HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict** cookie (30-day duration)

Browser type and version, operating system
Pages visited, features used, timestamps
Session data and client-side JWT tokens
Error logs and application traces (without personal data, in accordance with our logging policy)

Postal billing address
Billing email address
Intra-community VAT number (where applicable)
Subscription history and invoiced periods

subsections.title: 2.7 Communication and support data
list: Email exchanges with our support team
Support tickets, feature requests and incident reports
In-app notifications and transactional emails (account verification, password reset, quota alerts, billing notifications)

sections.title: Article 3 - Use of Personal Data
sections.intro: Your data are used exclusively for the following purposes:

subsections.title: 3.1 Provision of the CSR SaaS service
list: Creating and managing your User account and your Organisation
Authenticating you securely and managing your sessions (JWT + MFA)
Providing access to CSR management features: management of Pillars, Objectives, Projects, Actions, Milestones, KPIs, Risks and Ideas (WSJF)
Generating and making available exportable PowerPoint reports
Displaying dashboards, the Kanban view and the CSR calendar
Managing permissions and roles (RBAC) within your Organisation
Ensuring service continuity and backups

subsections.title: 3.2 Platform improvement
list: Analysing Platform usage in **anonymised** aggregate form only, without individual User identification
Developing, testing and deploying new features
Correcting technical anomalies and optimising performance
Improving the user experience

subsections.title: 3.3 Transactional and service communications
list: Sending account verification, password reset and invitation emails
Notifying quota alerts, Platform updates and contractual information
Responding to support requests and complaints
Communicating required legal and regulatory information

subsections.title: 3.4 Billing and commercial management
list: Issuing and transmitting invoices
Managing subscriptions, renewals and Plan upgrades
Recovering amounts due under the conditions set out in the Terms of Use
Complying with statutory accounting obligations

subsections.title: 3.5 Security and legal compliance
list: Detecting and preventing unauthorised access, intrusion attempts and abusive behaviour
Protecting the integrity of the Platform and the data of other Customers
Enforcing the Terms and Conditions of Use
Complying with legal obligations and orders from competent judicial or administrative authorities

sections.note: **What we do not do:** YUMNI SAS carries out no commercial profiling, no behavioural advertising targeting, no sale, rental or transfer of personal data to third parties for their own purposes. Your data are never used for purposes other than those listed above.

sections.title: Article 4 - Legal Basis for Processing
sections.intro: The processing of your personal data is based on the following legal grounds, in accordance with Article 6 of the GDPR:

subsections.title: 4.1 Performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b))
paragraphs: The majority of processing operations are necessary for the performance of the Terms and Conditions of Use that you have accepted, or for the performance of pre-contractual measures taken at your request. This includes in particular account creation, authentication, provision of CSR features, billing and transactional communications.

subsections.title: 4.2 Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c))
paragraphs: Certain processing operations are required by law, including in particular the retention of accounting documents and supporting records for ten (10) years pursuant to Article L.123-22 of the French Commercial Code, or the communication of data to judicial authorities in response to a legal order.

subsections.title: 4.3 Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f))
subsections.intro: We rely on the legitimate interest of YUMNI SAS for the following processing operations, which do not override your fundamental rights and freedoms in a strictly professional context:
list: Platform security and fraud prevention (access logs, anomaly detection, anti-brute force protection)
Continuous service improvement through the analysis of aggregated and anonymised usage data
Management and resolution of potential disputes

subsections.title: 4.4 Dual role of YUMNI SAS under the GDPR
subsections.intro: YUMNI SAS fulfils two legally distinct roles depending on the nature of the data processed:

labeledParagraphs.label: As data controller:
labeledParagraphs.text: for data relating to the management of User accounts, authentication, billing, support and commercial relations. This Privacy Policy applies directly to these processing operations.

labeledParagraphs.label: As data processor (Art. 28 GDPR):
labeledParagraphs.text: for operational CSR data imported, created and administered by the Customer in the Platform (projects, objectives, actions, KPIs, risks, ideas, reports, documents). In this capacity, YUMNI SAS processes these data only on the Customer's instructions, who remains the data controller. A Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is concluded automatically upon acceptance of the Terms of Use. YUMNI SAS undertakes never to exploit Customer Data for its own purposes.

sections.title: Article 5 - Data Sharing
sections.intro: YUMNI SAS undertakes **not to sell, rent or share your personal data** with third parties for commercial purposes.

subsections.title: 5.1 Authorised technical sub-processors
subsections.intro: We share your data only with the following technical service providers, strictly necessary for the provision of the service, bound to YUMNI SAS by contracts compliant with Article 28 of the GDPR:

rows: Application hosting, PostgreSQL databases, object storage (PPTX reports, GDPR archives)

subsections.title: 5.2 Legal recipients
subsections.intro: We may be required to disclose data to the following authorities, solely within the limits imposed by law:
list: **Judicial and administrative authorities** (courts, tax authorities, CNIL) in response to a requisition or legal order
**Legal counsel of YUMNI SAS** in the context of defending its rights in the event of a dispute, under an obligation of confidentiality

subsections.title: 5.3 In the event of a restructuring of YUMNI SAS
paragraphs: In the event of a merger, acquisition, sale of a business line or any other restructuring operation affecting YUMNI SAS, your data may be transferred to the acquirer or successor entity, provided that it complies with this Privacy Policy and that you are informed thereof in advance in accordance with the Terms of Use.

subsections.title: 5.4 No public sharing
paragraphs: The YUMNI Platform is a private, closed workspace. No personal data, no Customer Data and no CSR content is made public or shared with third parties outside the strictly defined perimeters set out above. A User of one Organisation cannot access the data of other Organisations.

sections.title: Article 6 - Data Retention Periods
sections.intro: YUMNI SAS applies retention periods strictly proportionate to the purposes pursued, in accordance with the storage limitation principle set out in Article 5(1)(e) of the GDPR.

subsections.title: 6.1 During the active contract period
paragraphs: All User account data and hosted Customer Data are retained for the entire duration of the active subscription and for as long as the account remains active.

subsections.title: 6.2 After termination or account deletion
list: **User account data:** permanently deleted within **30 days** of effective termination or deletion request, following a security grace period allowing recovery in the event of error

**Customer Data (operational CSR data):** the Customer has **30 days** from termination to export all their data via the Platform's export features; after this period, YUMNI SAS proceeds with their permanent and irreversible deletion
**Billing data and accounting records:** retained for **10 years** from the close of the relevant financial year, in accordance with Article L.123-22 of the French Commercial Code
**Security and access logs:** retained for **12 rolling months** for incident detection and forensic analysis purposes, then deleted
**Support exchanges:** retained for **3 years** from the closure of the request, in the legitimate interest of managing potential disputes

subsections.title: 6.3 Inactive Freemium accounts
paragraphs: Freemium accounts with no activity recorded for **24 consecutive months** may be subject to a closure procedure. YUMNI SAS will send a warning email to the account address at least **30 days** before any deletion. In the absence of a response within that period, the account and all associated data will be permanently deleted.

sections.title: Article 7 - Data Security
sections.intro: YUMNI SAS implements a comprehensive set of robust technical and organisational measures to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of your data, in accordance with Article 32 of the GDPR.

subgroups.label: Encryption and security protocols:
list: Encryption of all communications between browsers and the Platform via **HTTPS/TLS** (TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 recommended)
Passwords stored exclusively as irreversible hashes via **Bcrypt** (iteration factor 10–12) - no password is readable, even by YUMNI SAS
TOTP secrets (MFA) encrypted at rest via **AES-256-GCM**
MFA backup codes individually hashed
Authentication tokens **JWT signed with HMAC-SHA256**, 7-day validity, stateless server-side

subgroups.label: Access control and isolation:
list: **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)** verified on every HTTP request to the API: a User can only access the resources of their Organisation, within the limits of their role (OWNER, ADMIN, MANAGER, USER)
Strict data isolation between Organisations: no data from one Organisation is accessible to Users of another Organisation

subgroups.label: Protection against attacks:
list: Automatic account lockout after **3 consecutive failed MFA attempts** (5-minute lockout period)
Anti-bot protection on authentication forms via Cloudflare Turnstile
Systematic server-side validation of all incoming data via formal schemas (Zod)
HTTP security headers: Content Security Policy, HSTS, X-Frame-Options

subgroups.label: Logging without personal data:
list: Strict policy of **no personal data in application logs**: debug traces contain no email addresses, personal identifiers or Customer Data content

subsections.title: 7.2 Organisational measures
list: Internal data access strictly limited to YUMNI SAS personnel on a need-to-know (least privilege) basis
All sub-processors contractually bound by confidentiality and security obligations compliant with Article 28 of the GDPR
Regular Customer Data backup policy ensured by Scaleway SAS for service continuity

subsections.title: 7.3 Notification of data breaches
subsections.intro: In the event of a personal data breach likely to result in a risk to your rights and freedoms, YUMNI SAS undertakes to:
list: **Notify the CNIL** within **72 hours** of becoming aware of the breach, in accordance with Article 33 of the GDPR
**Inform you without undue delay** when the breach is likely to result in a high risk to your rights and freedoms, in accordance with Article 34 of the GDPR

subsections.title: 7.4 Your responsibility
paragraphs: Security also depends on your own vigilance. You are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of your password and MFA authentication devices. Never share them with third parties. Immediately report any unauthorised access or suspected compromise to dpo@yumni.fr (subject: [Security Incident]).

subsections.title: 8.1 Applicable framework
paragraphs: The YUMNI Platform is a SaaS application for strictly professional use. In accordance with the CNIL's recommendations on cookies and trackers, cookies that are strictly necessary for the secure operation of a service are exempt from the requirement to obtain prior consent.

rows: Secure memorisation of the trusted device for multi-factor authentication
Memorisation of the User's interface settings (language, active view)

subsections.title: 8.3 Anti-bot protection (Cloudflare Turnstile)
paragraphs: The Platform uses Cloudflare Turnstile on authentication forms to protect the service against automated attacks. This component may place technical session trackers for non-personal verification purposes. No identifiable personal data is transmitted to Cloudflare in this context.

subsections.title: 8.4 What we do not use
subsections.note: YUMNI SAS uses **no advertising cookies**, **no behavioural marketing trackers**, **no fingerprinting technology** for profiling purposes, and **no third-party analytics tools** collecting non-anonymised personal data. No advertising network receives any data relating to Platform Users.

subsections.title: 8.5 Cookie management
paragraphs: As the cookies listed above are strictly necessary for the operation and security of the Platform, disabling them via browser settings will result in the inability to access the service and maintain your authenticated session.

sections.title: Article 9 - Your GDPR Rights
sections.intro: In accordance with Articles 15 to 22 of the GDPR, you have the following rights regarding your personal data processed by YUMNI SAS in its capacity as **data controller**:

subsections.title: 9.1 Right of access (Art. 15 GDPR)
paragraphs: You may obtain confirmation that data concerning you are being processed by YUMNI SAS, as well as a copy of those data. You may access your data directly from the Platform interface, or by submitting a written request to our GDPR contact. We will respond within **30 days**.

subsections.title: 9.2 Right to rectification (Art. 16 GDPR)
paragraphs: You may correct or update your inaccurate, incomplete or outdated data directly via your account settings, or by contacting our support team.

subsections.title: 9.3 Right to erasure (Art. 17 GDPR)
paragraphs: You may request the deletion of your account and all your personal data. Deletion will take effect within **30 days** of your request, subject to applicable statutory retention obligations (in particular accounting data - see Article 6.2). After deletion, no restoration is possible.

subsections.title: 9.4 Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR)
paragraphs: You may request the temporary suspension of the processing of your data in the cases provided for by the GDPR (in particular where you contest the accuracy of your data or object to processing). The request must be submitted in writing.

subsections.title: 9.5 Right to data portability (Art. 20 GDPR)
paragraphs: You may request to receive your personal data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format. The Platform offers an export feature in a structured format, generating a secure access link valid for **48 hours**.

subsections.title: 9.6 Right to object (Art. 21 GDPR)
paragraphs: You may object, on grounds relating to your particular situation, to the processing of your data based on the legitimate interest of YUMNI SAS (see Article 4.3). Your request will be examined and we will cease the processing unless there are compelling legitimate grounds.

subsections.title: 9.7 Right not to be subject to solely automated decision-making (Art. 22 GDPR)
paragraphs: YUMNI SAS does not make any decision producing legal effects or significantly affecting you based solely on automated processing of your data. This right is fully respected by design.

subsections.title: 9.8 How to exercise your rights
subsections.intro: Please send your request to:
contactCard: **Subject line:** GDPR Request – [Access / Rectification / Erasure / Portability / Restriction / Objection]
**Response time:** maximum 30 days from receipt of a complete request (Art. 12 GDPR)
paragraphsAfter: YUMNI SAS may ask you to verify your identity in order to process your request in compliance with data security and third-party rights.

**Regarding Customer Data (operational CSR data):** for personal data that you may have integrated into your CSR workspaces, GDPR rights must be exercised directly with the **Customer** (the subscribing organisation), which is the data controller for those data. YUMNI SAS assists the Customer in responding to such requests within the statutory time limits.

subsections.title: 10.1 Hosting within the European Union
paragraphs: The vast majority of data processed by YUMNI SAS is **hosted and processed exclusively in France, within the European Union**, on the infrastructure of **Scaleway SAS** (fr-par region, Paris). These processing operations do not constitute international transfers within the meaning of Chapter V of the GDPR.

All Customer Data (operational CSR data) is stored on French territory. YUMNI SAS undertakes not to transfer any Customer Data outside the European Union without the Customer's prior and explicit consent.

subsections.title: 10.2 Transfers to third countries - Sub-processors established in the United States
subsections.intro: Two of our technical sub-processors are established in the United States. These transfers outside the European Economic Area (EEA) are governed by the following safeguards:

rows: Routing of transactional emails (account verification, password reset, notifications)
**Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs)** adopted by European Commission decision of 4 June 2021
Processing of the anti-bot signal (Cloudflare Turnstile) on authentication forms
**Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs)** adopted by European Commission decision of 4 June 2021

subsections.title: 10.3 Exceptional transfers
paragraphs: Should an unforeseen transfer of data outside the EEA become necessary for technical or legal reasons beyond the cases listed above, YUMNI SAS undertakes to implement in advance the appropriate safeguards provided for in Articles 46 et seq. of the GDPR (Standard Contractual Clauses, binding corporate rules, or any other safeguard recognised by European data protection authorities), and to inform the affected Customers accordingly.

sections.title: Article 11 - Reserved for Professionals - Exclusion of Minors
sections.intro: The YUMNI Platform is a SaaS solution for **exclusively professional** use, reserved for adult natural persons (at least **18 years of age**) acting in the course of their professional activity within a Customer organisation holding a current subscription.

subsections.title: 11.1 Prohibition of access by minors
paragraphs: Access to the Platform is **strictly prohibited for minors**, whether on a personal or professional basis. The Platform is not a consumer-facing service and is in no way directed at consumers or private individuals, regardless of age.

By subscribing to a plan or creating an account, you declare and warrant that you are of legal age and are acting in the course of your professional activity. If the law of the User's country of residence sets a higher age of majority for conducting an independent commercial or professional activity, that age shall apply.

subsections.title: 11.2 Detection and handling of non-compliant accounts
paragraphs: Should YUMNI SAS become aware that an account has been created by a minor or for strictly personal use, it will proceed with the **immediate suspension of the account** and the **permanent deletion of all associated data**, without notice or compensation. YUMNI SAS accepts no liability for any harm resulting from the provision of inaccurate information at account creation.

sections.title: Article 12 - Amendments to this Policy

Email to the account address + in-app notification
Editorial or clarifying amendment with no impact on rights
Publication of the revised version on the Platform with date indication
Amendment required by a legal or regulatory obligation
Upon entry into force of the legal obligation

subsections.title: 12.2 Acceptance of amendments
paragraphs: Continued use of the Platform after the effective date of a revised version of this Policy constitutes **acceptance** of that revised version.
If you disagree with a substantial amendment, you may delete your account and cease using the Platform before the amendment's effective date, without penalty in connection with that amendment.
